title: Care for Disabled and Elderly People

questions.q: In "Know your customer and market Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: List five rivals or substitutes within reach. For each, record price, strength, weakness and how people reach it.
Name the key resource at each stage: a trained carer and a care plan. Note what happens if it is missing.
In care for disabled and elderly people: Train carers in safe lifting, dignity, dementia basics and emergency response.
Check that insurance and legal duties match the risk you actually carry.

questions.q: In "Rules, registration and data duties in Brazil Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Plan the renewal of licences, equipment and skills a year ahead.
Create two options at most, so choice stays easy.
Personal data of customers falls under Brazil's data protection law (LGPD). Collect only what you need, say why, keep it safe, and name who answers questions.
Contribution per care day = price minus variable cost. Fixed costs are paid whether you sell or not.

questions.q: In "Design the offer Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Learn the tax regime that fits your size and write down which taxes you will collect and pay, and when.
Add one proof for each promise: a sample, a test result, a guarantee or a customer record.
Write who does what in an emergency, and rehearse it once a quarter.
Set one measurable target for 90 days, such as 'raise repeat customers from 20% to 30%'.

questions.q: In "Safety, quality and risk Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Choose one first segment and say why the others wait.
Write a simple one-page terms sheet: what is included, what is extra, how to cancel.
In care for disabled and elderly people: Falls, medication errors and neglect are core risks; use checklists and two-person checks.
Set service rules for answering customers: reply times, tone, how to apologise and fix.
